pr_body:
This flag mirrors `--experimental_check_output_files` to allow installations with a large number of external files to not scan them for changes on every bazel invocation.

If used in combination with `--experimental_check_output_files` and `--watchfs` you can now avoid scanning the cache for invalidations entirely allowing large projects to keep many things cached while still executing small `bazel run` commands quickly.

Fixes #14400

cc @susinmotion since you worked in here in 04dff44f530 more recently

Thinking a bit more about this, I can't see a reason why we would want to scan the filesystem for changes for anything from an `http_archive` or `git_repository`. Yes, for `local_repository` we absolutely should check the filesystem, but should I not make this a flag and instead just skip it all the time for those `bazel`-owned files?

@alexeagle pointed out that maybe scanning the file system by default is good for build reproducibility and this flag is only valuable in CI. Starting with a flag is the least impact so I guess starting here makes sense.
What about if you're using `--override_repository`? In that case does this disabling scanning for changes in those? In which case developing rule sets would be affected if you passed this

@keith yes, this would disable scanning those too since I think they would still be `EXTERNAL` files. But this flag is only intended for running `bazel` in environments where the filesystem is completely controlled by `bazel` (just like the corresponding `experimental_check_output_files `). We intend to use it in CI and not for people's local machines.

it might be nice to carve out that case if possible since then you could avoid that distinction. We use `experimental_check_output_files` for developers as well to reduce incremental build time, and would similarly like to use this if it worked well enough that someone would have to be doing something quite weird to break it.

Interesting point. I'm scared to enable it in dev as it won't guarantee
hermetic builds but I'm happy to exclude those since we obviously won't be
using them in CI.

Having said that, the main speedup here is not walking the whole cache
structure at all rather than skipping the filesystem stats so you'll lose
the speed if you have any of those overrides at all. So enabling it in dev
won't give you much.

Would the maintainers want me to set a bit if you have those and still do
the scan if they are present? I'm inclined to do that as a follow-up if
needed since that experience will be much slower.

The graph scan that causes you issues is guarded by https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/416ae3754f64cd86744c913e026eeb501555d6b0/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/SequencedSkyframeExecutor.java#L475-L479

Note that *any* external repo file encountered will pass the guard (which is why your flag is needed), but only `externalFilesKnowledge.tooManyNonOutputExternalFilesSeen` will pass the guard, not just *any* external non-repo file. The "too many" there is [2500](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/04dff44f5307aa4b0c74e09924f0a659d7debd02/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/ExternalFilesHelper.java#L46).

So, as long as your filesystem is --watchfs-compatible, and you aren't linking to thousands of other files that are neither in your workspace nor in external repositories, you can guarantee that none of the conditions in the guard are satisfied.
